To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the spin temperature of a DLA at $z = 2$ is low and that the HI 2cm absorption arises towards a component in the jet, rather than the optical sightline.

(1) we have detected HI 21cm line absorption in two high-$z$ damped Lyman-alpha systems, (2) the HI 21 cm optical depth is much higher than the Ly-alpha optical depth, (3) the HI 2 cm absorption is likely due to radio components in the radio jet, and (4) the spin temperature of the $z \approx$ 2 damped Lyman alpha system is lower than the spin temperature of high-$z$ systems

(1) the HI 21-cm absorption arises towards the radio jet in the DLA towards TX 1755+578 and (2) the DLA towards the compact radio source TXS1850 + 402 has a low spin temperature, which may be explained by a high metallicity
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the physical properties of the neutral gas in high redshift damped Lyman $\alpha$ systems (DLAs).
the study of the properties of the intergalactic medium and the evolution of the interstellar medium and galaxies.
understanding the nature of the neutral gas in high redshift galaxies, using HI 21cm observations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the spin temperature of the DLA towards TXs1850+402 is low, but the spin temperature of TXS1755 is uncertain due to the possibility that the radio jet is not aligned with the optical sightline.
the two new HI 18cm absorbers at redshifts of about 2, are associated with damped Lyman- $\alpha$ systems, and that one of these systems is associated with a jet.
these two new detections of 21cm absorptions in high column density dLAs are important for our understanding of the physical state of the neutral gas in these absorbers.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the new wide-band receivers onboard the GMRT are a powerful new tool in probing the physical conditions in high-$z$, high column density DLAs, and the GMRT is a valuable resource for the study of the neutral gas content in high-$z$.
the spin temperatures of high-$z$ absorbers are low, and that the spin temperature and metallicity are anti-correlated.

the spin temperature of the $z=2$ DLA towards radio-loud QSO TXS1850$+$402 is low, and the HI 21 cm absorption arises in the foreground DLA, while the $z= 2$ DLA toward the radio-loud QPO 1755$+$578 is highly obscured, and the HI absorption arises in the radio components of the jet.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the new wide-band receivers onboard the GMRT can be used for sensitive searches for HI 21cm emission/absorption at $z \gtrsim 1$.

with the new GMRT 250-500 MHz receivers, one can now routinely detect 21 cm absorption in high redshift DLAs with a sensitivity of $\sim 10$ mK km/s in a single 8 hr observation, with the ability to probe the kinematics and physical conditions in the absorbing gas.
the new GMRT receivers can detect HI 21cm in DLAs with column densities as low as ${\rm N(HI)} = 2 \times 10^{19}$ cm$^{-2}$ in a reasonable amount of time ($\approx 1$ day).
